dedupe_keys.name: flood hazard for new zealand flood plains by region

description: Earth Sciences New Zealand publishes nationally consistent floodplain hazard maps for a one-percent annual-exceedance-probability rainfall event. The maps represent current climate and conditions one, two and three degrees warmer, using 256 computational domains with four-metre output grids where LiDAR was available by December 2024. Outputs include maximum water depth and depth-velocity product, packaged by region and scenario as GeoTIFFs in ZIP files. Non-commercial use is free under CC-BY-NC; commercial restricted use carries published fees. The modelling accounts for existing stopbanks and combines river and direct-rainfall flooding. A limitation is that sea-level rise is excluded and antecedent catchment conditions remain based on present climate. The maps can screen infrastructure exposure and test adaptation priorities under increasing rainfall intensity. They complement the national hydrologically conditioned terrain dataset with modelled hazard surfaces. The public metadata was inspected, but the acquisition workflow and numerical maps were not tested.
